To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
monoclonal antibodies can be generated against protein dyes and that these antibodies are universal tools to detect prestained protein molecular mass markers.

1) monoclonal antibodies against the dye used for prestained marker proteins can be used to detect these markers in Western blot analyses, 2) these dye-specific antibodies can be used in combination with any antibody specific for a protein of interest, 3) the dye specific antibody can be used to simultaneously detect the prestained markers in a Western blot analysis and 4) these antibodies can be used to visualize even structurally related d yes not used in the antibody production.

we have developed a novel method to generate antibodies specific for dyes, and that these antibodies are universal tools to simultaneously visualize prestained protein molecular markers in Western blot analyses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel antibodies that allow the simultaneous detection and quantification of protein molecular weight markers.
the generation of antibodies against dyes that are used in the preparation of prestained molecular weight standards.
the development of a novel class of antibodies that can be applied in the field of molecular biology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the novel dye specific antibodies are a valuable addition to the toolbox of the molecular biologist and the antibody will be useful in many applications in the field of protein biochemistry and proteomics.
the novel anti-RAINBOWN antibodies are a valuable tool for the simultaneous Western-blot detection of prestained protein marker proteins and the protein of interest.
our novel antibodies will facilitate the simultaneous visualization of prestained proteins and the detection of specific protein of interest in chemiluminescence Western blot analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a universal tool to detect prestained protein molecular markers in the Western blot.
we have developed a novel approach for the generation of dye specific antibodies and that we have generated a novel universal antibody for the detection of prestained marker proteins.

our anti-dye antibodies allow to capture the marker proteins simultaneously with the specific protein of interest, which in combination with the use of a CCD camera and the software package ImageQuant TL will allow for an automated analysis of the Western blot.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of dye specific antibodies in the chemiluminscent detection of prestained marker proteins will greatly improve the accuracy of Western blotting.
the simultaneous visualization of prestained markers and specific proteins is feasible by the application of dye-specific antibodies.

the generation of dye-specific antibodies is not only a convenient tool to detect prestained protein molecular markers, but also a proof-of-concept for the development of dye-specific antibodies that can be used to visualize any dye in a wide range of applications.
